title: Perf Canary (Prod) — Launch Checklist (Phase 1 → Phase 2)
linked_artifacts: Confluence: ADR-0231 perf regression baseline strategy
Confluence: Runbook - perf canary regression triage
content:
Doc purpose
- This is the operational checklist to launch the Production Performance-Regression Canary (“perf-canary”) with safe rollout, clear ownership, and a repeatable rollback path.
- Scope: canary runner + metrics + dashboards + alerts + comms for phase expansions.
- Non-goal: replace offline benchmark lab. This is the prod detector + triage workflow.

Owners / escalation map (who does what)
- Program / timeline / go/no-go: Talia Benson
- Runtime perf triage (kernel/runtime changes): Noah Patel (backup: Hiro Tanaka)
- Scheduling variance / scheduler pinning: Sofia Ivanova
- Runtime instrumentation tags/fields: Omar El-Sayed
- Canary runner service (deploy + config): Marcus Reed
- Metrics / label schema / aggregation correctness: Nadia Rahman (backup: Logan Wright)
- Dashboards: Felix Schneider
- Alerting policy + PagerDuty hygiene: Sean Gallagher
- PagerDuty routing + incident-bot formatting: Rafael Mendes
- Release train coordination / deploy windows: Connor O’Brien
- Runbook quality + oncall training: Tomáš Novák

Launch prerequisites (must be true before any prod enabling)
[ ] Security/privacy check
    - Canary prompts are synthetic and contain no customer data.
    - Prompt set source is pinned (hash/commit) and review completed.
    - Logs do not record prompt contents (only prompt-set id + shape metadata).
    - Confirm retention/access controls for perf-canary metrics namespace.

[ ] Canary isolation / safety
    - “canary-safe” request class enabled (strict rate limits + priority controls).
    - Confirm canary cannot starve or contend with customer queues (verify via queue metrics).
    - Canary traffic tagged: source=perf-canary on all requests (runtime + gateway).

[ ] Runtime instrumentation is live (required dimensions)
    - runtime_build / runtime_version / git_sha available for canary requests.
    - scheduler_mode label present.
    - gpu_sku label present and validated (not “unknown”).
    - batch stats present (prefill/decode counts, max seq len, batch size).
    - kernel selection debug export gated behind canary tag (to control overhead).

[ ] Metric definitions & aggregation correctness
    - p95 latency computation verified end-to-end (runtime emission → pipeline → dashboard).
    - tokens/sec definition validated for streaming and non-streaming (first-token timestamp alignment fixed).
    - Minimum sample size logic agreed for alert evaluation.
    - Cardinality budget check passed: allowed labels only (model, region, gpu_sku, scheduler_mode, runtime_build, stream_mode, prompt_shape_id). No per-host labels.

[ ] Baseline strategy selected and configured
    - Baseline mode: rolling median (last 7d) OR pinned known-good build per slice.
    - Suppression rules are configured for deploy windows + warmup (see Deploy window handling).
    - Baseline backtest completed (estimate weekly pages).

[ ] Dashboards exist and are accessible
    - Perf-canary overview dashboard has:
        - per-model, per-region p95 latency panel
        - tokens/sec panel
        - heatmap by gpu_sku
        - annotations for runtime deploys
        - link-out to runbook and recent deploy diffs
    - Access for SRE + Runtime oncall confirmed (INT ticket done if needed).

[ ] Alert rules and routing are staged + tested
    - Alert dedup keys confirmed (group by model+region+gpu_sku+stream_mode; include runtime_build in payload, not in grouping).
    - Severity mapping confirmed (page vs ticket) for Phase 1.
    - PagerDuty service exists + test page acknowledged by SRE oncall.
    - Incident-bot posts to #eng-oncall with structured fields (dashboard link, runtime SHA, slice info).

[ ] Runbook is final enough to use at 03:00
    - “What to do first” checklist present.
    - Has steps to validate signal quality + confirm regression vs noise.
    - Has rollback and mitigation paths.
    - Includes how to file follow-up tuning tasks.


Phase 1 rollout plan (target: us-east, 2–3 models)
Target coverage (initial)
- Region: us-east
- Models: start with 2–3 from the curated list (choose a mix: one high-traffic family + one long-context-ish shape).
- Modes: streaming + non-streaming
- Prompt shapes: canonical set per model family (small, medium, long prefill; constrained decode)
- Scheduler: pinned (disable experimental heuristic X) to reduce variance and improve attribution.

Go/No-Go checklist (Phase 1 enabling)
[ ] Confirm today is NOT a major runtime deploy day (or set maintenance window suppression).
[ ] Confirm current runtime build is stable (“known-good”) for at least 24h in us-east.
[ ] Confirm perf-canary runner has global rate cap and per-model cap.
[ ] Confirm quotas/credentials for runner are production-scoped and least-privilege.
[ ] Confirm dashboards show non-empty timeseries for at least 2 hours in us-east.
[ ] Confirm alerting is initially set to “ticket-first” or “page-low” mode per SRE policy.

Execution steps (Phase 1)
1) Configure perf-canary runner
    [ ] Set region=us-east
    [ ] Set model allowlist (2–3 models)
    [ ] Set stream_mode: both
    [ ] Set prompt_shape_id allowlist
    [ ] Set request rate (start very low; ramp up once stable)
    [ ] Enable warmup + cache priming mode (if configured for stability)
    [ ] Confirm tags: source=perf-canary, canary_safe=true

2) Deploy perf-canary runner to prod
    [ ] Deploy to us-east only
    [ ] Verify runner health checks
    [ ] Verify error rates (HTTP/gRPC) are near zero and not spiking

3) Validate metrics in first 30–60 minutes
    [ ] p95 latency charts look plausible (no zeros, no NaNs, stable aggregation window)
    [ ] tokens/sec charts look plausible and align with rough expected ranges
    [ ] Labels present: model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode, stream_mode
    [ ] No obvious label explosion (check top-N series counts)

4) Enable alerts (progressive)
    [ ] Enable detector in “notify-only” for first N hours (per SRE guidance)
    [ ] After stability, switch on paging for high-confidence regressions only
    [ ] Confirm alert payload includes:
        - model + region + gpu_sku + stream_mode + prompt_shape_id
        - baseline used (rolling vs pinned) and baseline value
        - regression magnitude (%)
        - runtime_build + git_sha
        - links: dashboard + runbook + recent deploy diff

5) Announce Phase 1
    [ ] Post to #eng-runtime and #eng-oncall:
        - what is live (us-east, which models)
        - what pages mean (regression vs baseline)
        - where to look (dashboard + runbook)
        - who is primary/secondary owner

Phase 1 monitoring checklist (daily for first week)
- Signal quality
  [ ] Check number of samples per slice meets minimum for p95 stability
  [ ] Confirm warmup behavior not contaminating baseline
  [ ] Confirm no periodic dips correlated with known batcher/scheduler cycles

- Overhead / safety
  [ ] Verify canary request volume stays within cap
  [ ] Verify canary-safe class not impacting customer queue latency
  [ ] Verify runtime overhead from extra metrics remains within budget

- Alert hygiene
  [ ] Triage every alert: true regression vs false positive
  [ ] If false positive: identify root (deploy window, missing label, aggregation mismatch, contention)
  [ ] File tuning tasks (thresholds, suppression, prompt shape adjustments)


Phase 2 rollout plan (eu-west + more models)
Pre-Phase 2 requirements
[ ] Phase 1 stable for at least 5–7 days (no major open issues).
[ ] Baseline strategy confirmed to work across slices.
[ ] GPU SKU slicing validated (eu-west differs; must not mix SKUs in same series).
[ ] Maintenance window policy agreed for regional runtime rollouts.

Execution steps (Phase 2)
1) Expand runner config
    [ ] Add region=eu-west
    [ ] Add models (incrementally; avoid adding too many at once)
    [ ] Confirm prompt shapes still representative and stable for each new model family

2) Validate slice correctness
    [ ] Confirm gpu_sku label is correct in eu-west
    [ ] Confirm scheduler_mode pinning applied in eu-west

3) Expand alerting
    [ ] Start notify-only in eu-west for first 24h
    [ ] Enable paging after baseline stabilizes and sample counts are adequate

4) Comms
    [ ] Post to #announcements (internal) when Phase 2 is on
    [ ] Update “coverage” in the overview doc (regions/models)


Deploy window handling / suppressions
- We suppress (or degrade severity) during known deploy windows to prevent pages on expected warmups.
Checklist
[ ] Release train publishes deploy window schedule (Connor)
[ ] Maintenance windows configured in alerting for:
    - regional runtime rollouts
    - kernel autotune refresh events (if any)
    - planned cluster maintenance that affects GPU availability
[ ] Dashboards show deploy annotations (runtime_version + git_sha)
[ ] After deploy completes, ensure suppression ends automatically (no permanent silencing)


Regression response (summary)
When a perf-canary regression alert fires:
1) Validate signal quality
   - Is sample size sufficient? Any missing labels? Any ingestion lag?
   - Is this isolated to one gpu_sku or one scheduler_mode?
2) Correlate with deploy
   - Did runtime_build change recently? Is there a known deploy annotation?
3) Compare slices
   - us-east vs eu-west, gpu_sku A vs B, stream vs non-stream
4) If confirmed regression
   - Page Runtime owner if not already involved
   - Capture context: kernel selection dump (canary-gated), scheduler queue metrics, batch stats
   - Decide mitigation: rollback runtime build in impacted region OR disable experimental feature flag
5) If suspected noise
   - Adjust suppression/thresholding carefully; file follow-up tuning ticket


Rollback plan (must be executable in < 30 minutes)
Rollback triggers (examples)
- Canary runner is causing measurable customer impact (queue contention, elevated error rates).
- Canary emits excessive cardinality or pipeline cost.
- Alerts are paging noisily and cannot be suppressed quickly.

Rollback steps
A) Stop the runner safely
[ ] Set runner rate to 0 (config) OR disable job in region
[ ] Confirm canary request volume drops to ~0
[ ] Confirm customer queue metrics return to baseline

B) Disable alerting
[ ] Temporarily disable paging rules (leave dashboards on)
[ ] Keep notify-only if needed for debugging
[ ] Post to #eng-oncall explaining the disablement + owner/timebox

C) Disable high-overhead instrumentation (if needed)
[ ] Turn off kernel-selection debug export (canary gated) if overhead suspected
[ ] Verify CPU overhead in serving runtime drops

D) Post-rollback follow-up
[ ] Create Linear tickets with root cause + next steps
[ ] Schedule quick retro (15–30 min) with Runtime + SRE + Telemetry


Ownership handoff (steady-state)
- After Phase 2, perf-canary becomes a standard production detector.
Handoff checklist
[ ] SRE oncall owns initial alert receipt + confirms signal quality.
[ ] Runtime oncall owns regression root cause + mitigation decisions.
[ ] Telemetry oncall (business hours) owns metric pipeline/label issues.
[ ] Runbook updated with current paging policy + updated dashboards.
[ ] Add perf-canary to oncall training deck + rotation onboarding.


Comms plan
Phase 1 announcement (internal)
- Channel: #eng-runtime, #eng-oncall
- Include:
  - Coverage: us-east + model list
  - What triggers pages
  - Dashboard + runbook links
  - Escalation owners

Phase 2 announcement (broader)
- Channel: #announcements, plus targeted eng channels
- Include:
  - Coverage expansion (eu-west + additional models)
  - Reminder about maintenance window behavior
  - How to request dashboard access

Operational changes / maintenance notifications
- Any planned silencing or detector threshold changes:
  [ ] Post in #eng-oncall with start/end time and reason
  [ ] Document in change log section below


Change log (edit this doc)
- 2026-02-05: Added streaming tokens/sec definition reminder (first-token timestamp alignment).
- 2026-02-11: Updated routing: SRE pages first, Runtime auto-assigned after confirmation.
- 2026-02-18: Added explicit rollback steps for disabling kernel debug export + runner rate-to-zero.

Open questions / TODO (before Phase 2)
- Do we want pinned known-good baseline for specific model+gpu_sku slices with high sensitivity?
- What is the minimum sample size per slice that gives stable p95 without hiding short regressions?
- How do we represent mixed-load effects without reintroducing high variance (separate workload mix profile in v2)?
- Should Phase 2 start with notify-only for longer in eu-west due to known GPU heterogeneity?
